about: Every picture the Creatives space uses (docs/creatives-plan.md §9 and design turn 31's Assets note). Made by hand in the Gemini app, saved into inbox/ as <id>.png, then imported with python3 -I prototypes/japanese-space/art_import.py art-source/creatives assets/creatives/img, and each imported id listed in KOS_CR.ART (js/data/creatives.js). The prompt sheet is prototypes/creatives-space/art.html. Writing and Graphic design need no pictures: their examples are words and type, drawn live (no image ever holds text). These are Art units 1-3's: four step pictures a lesson, each showing EXACTLY the step its caption names, and one expected beginner output, which must look like a genuine beginner's pass, never polished.

styles.step: STYLE: A clean instructional drawing for a beginner's drawing course, on plain off-white paper seen flat from straight above; the paper fills the frame. Graphite pencil only: the lines this step adds in confident dark pencil, everything from earlier steps in a light, thin grey pencil. Construction and guide lines in a light blue pencil. No shading, no hands unless the step names one, no colour except the light blue. Generous empty paper around the drawing.
styles.beginner: STYLE: A real page from a complete beginner's sketchbook, photographed flat from straight above in soft daylight: graphite pencil on slightly textured cheap sketchbook paper. Honest beginner lines: a little wobbly, some overshoots, a few doubled strokes and smudges, but clearly attempting the exercise. Never polished, never professional. Match the paper and pencil of the attached step image.
styles.spot: STYLE: Match the rendering of the attached style reference (painterly modern anime illustration, soft cel shading, gentle lighting from the front-left, rich but slightly muted colours). Do NOT draw the woman from the style reference; use her only for the art style.

rules: Never any text: no letters, numbers, labels, arrows with words, captions, signatures or logos. Step numbers and captions are added in the app as live text.
A step picture shows EXACTLY the step its caption names: nothing from a later step.
A beginner page looks like a genuine first try that passes this unit's one skill, never polished art.

batches.title: The style anchor
batches.why: Step 3 of A3.1 (one-point perspective), chosen because it shows everything the style needs: the paper, dark and light pencil, and blue guide lines. Every other step and beginner page attaches it, so regenerate until it looks right.

batches.title: Step pictures, Art units 1-3
batches.why: Four a lesson for A1.1-A3.3. Attach the anchor; check each shows only its own step.

batches.title: Expected beginner outputs
batches.why: One a lesson: honest, wobbly, passing. If one looks too good, ask for it rougher.

batches.title: Empty-state spots
batches.why: Three small pictures for the empty Portfolio, the empty Practice Log and a rest day, on flat green (keyed out on import).

assets.caption: Lines from its corners to the point
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.1, "One-point perspective", step 3 of 4: "Lines from its corners to the point". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same rectangle with light straight lines from each of its corners running to the vanishing point.

assets.caption: Two dots for the line's start and end
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.1, "Ghosted lines", step 1 of 4: "Two dots for the line's start and end". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: two small pencil dots on the page, about a hand's width apart, nothing else drawn yet.

assets.caption: Ghost the motion above the paper
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.1, "Ghosted lines", step 2 of 4: "Ghost the motion above the paper". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same two dots; a hand holding a pencil hovers just above the page, and a faint dotted trail in the air shows the motion repeated between the dots.

assets.caption: Draw it from the shoulder in one stroke
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.1, "Ghosted lines", step 3 of 4: "Draw it from the shoulder in one stroke". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the two dots now joined by one straight, confident pencil line, slightly darker at both ends where the stroke started and stopped.

assets.caption: A page of lines in every direction
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.1, "Ghosted lines", step 4 of 4: "A page of lines in every direction". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a whole page of straight ghosted lines between dot pairs, in many directions, all confident; the newest line is darkest.

assets.caption: A flat rectangle for the ellipse to sit in
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.2, "Ellipses", step 1 of 4: "A flat rectangle for the ellipse to sit in". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: one long, flat pencil rectangle, lightly drawn.

assets.caption: Ghost the round motion inside it
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.2, "Ellipses", step 2 of 4: "Ghost the round motion inside it". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same rectangle; a faint dotted oval trail inside it, touching the middle of each side, showing the motion rehearsed.

assets.caption: Go round two or three times in one go
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.2, "Ellipses", step 3 of 4: "Go round two or three times in one go". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a smooth ellipse inside the rectangle, drawn as two or three loose overlapping loops in one stroke, touching each side once.

assets.caption: A column of ellipses, thin to round
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.2, "Ellipses", step 4 of 4: "A column of ellipses, thin to round". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a vertical column of six ellipses from very thin at the top to nearly circular at the bottom, each with its long axis horizontal and a light straight line through its short axis.

assets.caption: Three dots for the start, the bend and the end
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.3, "Curves that commit", step 1 of 4: "Three dots for the start, the bend and the end". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: three small pencil dots laid out on a gentle arc.

assets.caption: Ghost the curve through the dots
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.3, "Curves that commit", step 2 of 4: "Ghost the curve through the dots". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the three dots with a faint dotted curved trail rehearsing the motion through them.

assets.caption: One smooth C curve
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.3, "Curves that commit", step 3 of 4: "One smooth C curve". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the three dots joined by one smooth, confident C-shaped curve.

assets.caption: S curves: the bend changes side
assets.prompt: Art lesson A1.3, "Curves that commit", step 4 of 4: "S curves: the bend changes side". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a row of four smooth S-shaped curves, each through its own set of dots, the curve changing direction once in the middle.

assets.caption: The nearest corner as a Y
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.1, "A box drawn through", step 1 of 4: "The nearest corner as a Y". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: three short straight pencil lines meeting at one point like a letter Y with a vertical stem: the nearest corner of a box.

assets.caption: The top face's far edges
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.1, "A box drawn through", step 2 of 4: "The top face's far edges". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the Y now closed at the top into a flat four-sided top face, its opposite edges roughly parallel.

assets.caption: The side edges down
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.1, "A box drawn through", step 3 of 4: "The side edges down". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the vertical edges dropped from the top face's outer corners and the two bottom edges added, making a solid-looking box.

assets.caption: The hidden edges, drawn through
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.1, "A box drawn through", step 4 of 4: "The hidden edges, drawn through". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same box with its three hidden back edges drawn through in a lighter pencil line, meeting at the hidden back corner.

assets.caption: A box seen straight from the front
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.2, "Boxes that turn", step 1 of 4: "A box seen straight from the front". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a single box drawn through, seen almost face on, mostly its front face with a thin top.

assets.caption: The same box turned a little
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.2, "Boxes that turn", step 2 of 4: "The same box turned a little". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same box turned slightly to the right, a narrow side face now showing, hidden edges drawn through.

assets.caption: Turned further, both sides showing
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.2, "Boxes that turn", step 3 of 4: "Turned further, both sides showing". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same box turned so both side faces show about equally, the nearest vertical edge in the middle, hidden edges drawn through.

assets.caption: Seen from above
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.2, "Boxes that turn", step 4 of 4: "Seen from above". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same box seen from higher up, the top face large, hidden edges drawn through.

assets.caption: A tall box as the guide
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.3, "Cylinders from boxes", step 1 of 4: "A tall box as the guide". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: one tall, narrow box drawn through in light pencil.

assets.caption: An ellipse in the top and bottom faces
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.3, "Cylinders from boxes", step 2 of 4: "An ellipse in the top and bottom faces". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same light box with an ellipse drawn inside its top face and another inside its bottom face, each touching the middle of the face's sides.

assets.caption: The two side lines, touching both ellipses
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.3, "Cylinders from boxes", step 3 of 4: "The two side lines, touching both ellipses". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: two straight vertical lines joining the outer edges of the two ellipses, making a cylinder inside the box.

assets.caption: The back of the base drawn through
assets.prompt: Art lesson A2.3, "Cylinders from boxes", step 4 of 4: "The back of the base drawn through". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the finished cylinder with the hidden back half of the bottom ellipse drawn through, the guide box faint.

assets.caption: A horizon line and one vanishing point
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.1, "One-point perspective", step 1 of 4: "A horizon line and one vanishing point". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a long horizontal pencil line across the page with one small dot on it near the centre.

assets.caption: A rectangle facing you
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.1, "One-point perspective", step 2 of 4: "A rectangle facing you". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same line and dot, with one flat rectangle drawn below and to the left of the dot, its sides perfectly horizontal and vertical.

assets.caption: The back edge cut: a box
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.1, "One-point perspective", step 4 of 4: "The back edge cut: a box". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the lines cut off by a smaller back rectangle parallel to the front one, making a box receding to the point, the rest of the guide lines faint.

assets.caption: A horizon with two points far apart
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.2, "Two-point perspective", step 1 of 4: "A horizon with two points far apart". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a long horizontal pencil line with one dot near each end of the page, far apart.

assets.caption: The nearest vertical edge
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.2, "Two-point perspective", step 2 of 4: "The nearest vertical edge". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same line and dots with one short vertical line standing a little below the horizon between them.

assets.caption: Lines from its ends to both points
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.2, "Two-point perspective", step 3 of 4: "Lines from its ends to both points". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: light straight lines from the top and bottom of that vertical edge running to both vanishing points.

assets.caption: The back verticals: a box
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.2, "Two-point perspective", step 4 of 4: "The back verticals: a box". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: two more vertical edges cutting the guide lines on each side, and the box's top completed, the guide lines faint.

assets.caption: A horizon and one vanishing point
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.3, "A street of boxes", step 1 of 4: "A horizon and one vanishing point". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: a horizontal pencil line across the page with one dot in the middle.

assets.caption: The road's two edges to the point
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.3, "A street of boxes", step 2 of 4: "The road's two edges to the point". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: two straight lines from the bottom corners of the page running to the vanishing point, making a road.

assets.caption: Boxes along the road as buildings
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.3, "A street of boxes", step 3 of 4: "Boxes along the road as buildings". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: simple tall boxes standing on both sides of the road, their side edges running to the vanishing point, getting smaller as they recede.

assets.caption: Windows that follow the lines
assets.prompt: Art lesson A3.3, "A street of boxes", step 4 of 4: "Windows that follow the lines". Draw exactly this step and nothing beyond it: the same street with rows of simple rectangular windows on the buildings' sides, their top and bottom edges following lines to the vanishing point.

Art lesson A1.1, "Ghosted lines": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: a page of about twenty ghosted lines between dot pairs, most straight but a few wobble at the end, two overshoot their dots, one is drawn twice.

Art lesson A1.2, "Ellipses": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: a column of eight ellipses from thin to round; several are lopsided, one has a pointed end, most are traced round two or three times, the short-axis lines are slightly off centre.

Art lesson A1.3, "Curves that commit": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: a page of C and S curves through dots; most are smooth, a few have a flat spot or a small kink where the stroke slowed, one is gone over twice.

Art lesson A2.1, "A box drawn through": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: three boxes drawn through on one page; their back edges meet a little off, one box looks slightly bent because its edges spread apart, the hidden lines are as dark as the front ones.

Art lesson A2.2, "Boxes that turn": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: a row of five boxes turning step by step; the turn reads, but the third box's top face is too tall and the last box tips slightly forward.

Art lesson A2.3, "Cylinders from boxes": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: four cylinders in their guide boxes; the bottom ellipses are a little too flat compared with the top, one cylinder leans, the side lines slightly miss the ellipses' edges.

Art lesson A3.1, "One-point perspective": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: a horizon with one point and four boxes around it; most edges aim at the point but two miss it slightly, and one box's back face is not quite parallel to its front.

Art lesson A3.2, "Two-point perspective": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: three boxes in two-point perspective on one horizon; one box looks stretched because its sides run too far, one back vertical leans slightly, the guide lines are left heavy.

Art lesson A3.3, "A street of boxes": a complete beginner's practice page for this lesson, the honest result of a first try: a one-point street of simple box buildings; it reads as a street, but a few windows don't follow the perspective lines, one building's roof line points above the horizon.
